examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, you have visitors! Ta-da!

in greetings: добрый день, добрый вечер

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!

meanings.note: + infinitive. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

meanings.note: Подожди! = wait!. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to wait (a while)', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: С половиной = and a half. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ловина'). Common feminine noun meaning 'half' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Three and a half per mille?

examples.text: Три с половиной промилле? У меня семь кредитов!
examples.trans: Three and a half per mille? I have seven loans!

meanings.note: К сожалению = unfortunately. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ожаление'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'regret, pity' in everyday Russian.
